reports.title: Russia's Tactical Nuclear Threshold: Low, Rising, and Concentrated in the Compound Path
reports.om: NERAI assesses Russian tactical nuclear use within 12 months at 3-6% (structured low-confidence estimate, derivation published) - roughly an order of magnitude above any pre-2022 baseline, concentrated where battlefield reversal compounds with regime stress (15-30% in that branch).
reports.summary: Five use-preparation indicators, one honest reading: warhead production quiet (no evidence of large-scale non-strategic growth; rate unknown), custody rehearsed but not enacted (the May 2026 unannounced exercise filmed dummy-warhead transfer to a Belarusian Iskander unit), exercises institutionalizing, rhetoric plateaued, context triggers converging slowly. A qualitatively larger Russian offensive is not the base case (15-25%): ground-force stock has grown (ATA 2026) but the flow - recruitment intake, casualty-per-gain, armour storage - is deteriorating. Internal strain (persisting fuel crisis; Levada June 2026: 64% back negotiations, 29% back continuing) is a conditional risk multiplier, not yet a pathway: no evidence of elite fracture or regime-security alarm. Every probability is a labelled analyst judgment with its assumptions table in the full version; single-origin claims (the DPRK deployment picture) are flagged as unverified.
findings: The quiet indicator: ~1,794 non-strategic warheads (FAS 2026), no evidence of large-scale increase - and with ~1,800 already in inventory, stasis says little about limited-use intent.
The moving indicator: the unannounced 19-21 May 2026 exercise rehearsed physical warhead transfer to a Belarusian Iskander unit on film - capability practice, not enactment.
The scenario grid: grinding continuation 50-60% (TNW 1-3%; 4-8% with internal shock), freeze 15-20%, major reversal 12-18% (TNW 8-15%; 15-30% compounded), Russian success 8-16%. Weighted: ~3-6%.

The compound path is the planner's cell: by weight of probability the grinding branch carries the largest share of total risk - slow failure plus internal rupture gives less warning than the cinematic scenario.

Watchlist discipline: 12th GUMO movement outside exercises, Belarus visual confirmation, mobilization signals, elite coercion (NERAI confiscate-property at 98th pct, +53), fuel-fiscal markers, decision-maker specificity.

reports.title: US-Iran Conflict, American Public Opinion & the 2026 Midterm Election Outlook
reports.om: NERAI assesses the US-Iran conflict as a net electoral liability for President Trump and congressional Republicans: no rally effect has materialised, energy costs are feeding economic dissatisfaction, and independents are breaking against the incumbent. Base case: Democrats recapture the House (62%); Republicans narrowly hold the Senate (58%).
reports.summary: Five months into the US-Iran war, NERAI finds no 'rally-around-the-flag' dividend for Trump: net approval is flat-to-negative, Brent is up ~12% in 30 days to ~$89, and the Strait of Hormuz is running -73% vs baseline (SEVERE). The report reads the 2026 midterms as a competence referendum decided by suburban independents, with a base case of Democratic House control and Republican Senate retention, conditional on no escalation shock in the final 90 days. Rev. 1.1 corrects the 2026 Senate map and attributes the 31 July Damietta (Egypt) drone strike as unclaimed.
findings: No rally, rising costs: unlike 1991 (Bush ~89%) or post-9/11 (Bush ~86%), Trump has seen no durable approval bounce; Brent +~12%/30d to ~$89 and Hormuz -73% (SEVERE) turn conflict into a pocketbook issue for swing-state voters.

House base case - Democratic recapture (62%): a ~10-seat Republican net loss (range -6 to -18), below the historical ~28-seat midterm penalty thanks to a redistricting buffer, but enough to flip control; decisive in ~3-5 suburban toss-ups.

Senate base case - Republicans hold (58%): on a corrected 2026 map, the competitive seats are Democratic-held Georgia (Ossoff) and open Michigan/New Hampshire, and Republican-held Maine, open North Carolina and the Ohio special - Montana, Ohio and West Virginia are Republican-held, and Arizona/Pennsylvania are not on the 2026 Senate ballot.

The tail risk: a single high-casualty escalation shock (aircraft downed, Hormuz mining, Iranian strike on Saudi oil) in the final 90 days could flip the dynamic - NERAI's Iran Military Escalation index is RISING; the 31 July Damietta drone strike was unclaimed and is not attributed to Iran.

reports.title: Saudi Arabia's Oil Corridors Under Pressure: The Hormuz Alternative Is Now Contested
reports.type: Energy Corridor / Supply Chain Risk Assessment
reports.om: Strait of Hormuz throughput is -72% below baseline (SEVERE) - the most disrupted chokepoint in NERAI's global tracking - forcing Saudi Arabia onto its Red Sea alternative just as that route comes under two-front pressure from Iran-aligned militias in Iraq and Yemen's Houthis.
reports.summary: Saudi Arabia built the Petroline-Yanbu-Red Sea route to survive a Hormuz closure; in July 2026 both ends of that alternative are under pressure at once. NERAI data (27 Jul 2026): Hormuz throughput -72.3% (SEVERE); Red Sea/Bab-el-Mandeb corridor escalation 53.7/100 with throughput still near normal (+4.2%) - the squeeze is real on threat and insurance, not yet on physical flow. Iran (Military Clash/Escalation 92nd pct), Yemen (Intl. Threats 97th) and Iraq (Mil. Clash 82nd) all register RISING military signals. The pattern is leverage, not shutdown.
findings: The signal (Hormuz collapse): Strait of Hormuz vessel throughput is -72.3% below baseline (SEVERE) - the single most disrupted chokepoint in NERAI's global tracking (next-worst Bosporus at -12.9%) - forcing operational dependence on the Red Sea corridor.

The two-front backdrop (in the data): Iran Military Clash and Military Escalation both at the 92nd percentile, Yemen International Threats at the 97th, Iraq Military Clash at the 82nd - all RISING - confirming a coordinated north (Iraq militia) and south (Houthi) pressure geometry rather than a single-corridor event.

The nuance (threat vs flow divergence): NERAI's Red Sea/Bab-el-Mandeb corridor shows elevated escalation pressure (53.7/100) while chokepoint throughput remains near normal (+4.2%) - risk is being priced into threat and war-risk insurance faster than into physical flows. That gap is the leading indicator to watch.

The read (leverage, not shutdown): The aim is to make every Saudi barrel costlier and less predictable to move, not to halt production. Scenario judgment (analyst estimate, not model output): controlled harassment 55% / one-corridor closure 30% / de-escalation 15% over a 30-day horizon.

reports.title: India's July 2026 Instability Spike: Legislative Disruption, Not Regime Fracture
reports.om: India's political-instability indices hit the highest readings in NERAI's series history in the week of 15–22 July — political dissent and opposition activeness at 90.9/100 (100th percentile). The verified driver is a protest-and-parliament cycle around the NEET-UG paper-leak controversy, not a coalition collapse.
reports.summary: India's instability indices hit series-history highs in the week of 15–22 July (dissent and opposition activeness 90.9/100, +13σ). Verified drivers: the NEET-UG paper-leak controversy stalling both Houses from 20 July, student protests, and the 21 July detention of Rahul and Priyanka Gandhi with multi-state Congress protests. NERAI's read: a bounded legislative-session clash — Crisis-regime persistence ~3.9 days, 12-month forecast −50 to −73%, head-of-government change within 180 days under 5%. The risk is legislative-efficiency degradation and durable opposition coordination, not government collapse.
findings: The signal (record prints): political_dissent and opposition_activeness at 90.9/100 (100th percentile, +13σ), government_instability at 49.5/100 — the most extreme domestic-dissent cluster in NERAI's India series, with a verified changepoint in week 27.

The verified driver: the NEET-UG paper-leak controversy — both Houses stalled from the session's opening on 20 July, demands for Education Minister Pradhan's resignation, student protests met with police action, and the 21 July detention of Rahul and Priyanka Gandhi followed by protests across 5+ states.

The institutional read: a 293-seat NDA, an intact Cabinet and zero coalition-defection signals. HMM 'Crisis' regime persistence is ~3.9 days — Crisis is the model's top state, so the informative signal is the short expected stay, not the (structurally zero) escalation probability. The closest analog (2026-W08) eased within 8 weeks.

The outlook: mean-reversion base case 55% (indices back to 40–50 range within 2–4 weeks); exam-integrity escalation risk case 32%; discrete-shock tail 13% per the calibrated model. Head-of-government change within 90–180 days: under 5% (HIGH CONFIDENCE).

reports.title: Three Corridors, Three Risk Channels — July 2026
reports.summary: Black Sea, Malacca and Taiwan Strait: container and dry-bulk pressure sit in the low-to-medium 40s across all three, yet each transmits commercial risk through a different channel. Black Sea = sanctions, re-export corridors (Severe 84–90/100) and shadow-fleet enforcement (index 45.0/100, Moderate/falling) with transit strained ‑10.8%. Malacca = quiet chokepoint carrying the highest news signal of the three (83.0/100) plus Indonesia natural-hazard exposure — a monitoring story, not a panic story. Taiwan Strait = normal transit (+6.9%) but the largest strategic tail-risk via China sanctions (32.0/100), Section 301 tariff exposure and semiconductor dependency. The absence of a freight shock is not the absence of risk.
reports.om: Black Sea, Malacca and Taiwan Strait: freight pressure is contained across all three — but each transmits commercial risk through a different channel, and it can surface before it ever shows up in freight rates.
findings: Contained freight, divergent risk (HIGH confidence): container and dry-bulk pressure sit in the low-to-medium 40s across all three corridors — yet each carries material exposure through a distinct non-price channel: sanctions and shadow-fleet enforcement (Black Sea), systemic chokepoint dependency (Malacca), and strategic tail-risk (Taiwan Strait).

Black Sea — the sanctions corridor: transit strained ‑10.8% and a live Russia-Ukraine flashpoint, with re-export/circumvention routes rated Severe (China/Hong Kong→Russia 90/100, Armenia 88, Kyrgyzstan 86, UAE 84). Shadow-fleet enforcement pressure sits at 45.0/100 (Moderate, falling) but remains active.

Malacca — quiet chokepoint, systemic dependency: operationally calm (transit ‑4.7%, escalation 5.4, zero port incidents) but the highest news signal of the three (83.0/100) plus Red-level earthquake exposure around Indonesia. A monitoring story, not a panic story.

Taiwan Strait — normal transit, largest tail-risk: transit +6.9% and low escalation, yet a China sanctions signal at 32.0/100, Section 301 tariff exposure (EVs +100%, solar/semiconductors +50%) and the semiconductor / South China Sea overlay make the strategic downside the largest of the three.

reports.title: Russia–Poland Escalation Risk — July 2026
reports.summary: Will Russia move against Poland? Not a full invasion (HIGH confidence), but the groundwork for a limited, deniable border provocation to test NATO Article 5 credibility. Base case: a time-bound Poland–Kaliningrad / Suwałki incident within 90 days (45%). Tension 28.1/100 (91st pctile, +8.5/7d); Military Clash & Escalation at the 95th percentile; Russia in NERAI's 'Crisis' regime.

reports.title: Shadow Fleet Enforcement Risk — June 2026
reports.summary: Russia's shadow-fleet oil trade: enforcement pressure is tightening at the margins (NERAI index 35/100, Stable) but cost transmission stays weak while revenue holds at ~€726mn/day. Black Sea is the only Act-driven corridor; threat-vs-act phase, cost-transmission channels and an underwriter checklist.

reports.title: Supply-Chain Disruption Outlook — June 2026
reports.summary: A synchronized three-vector shock: the Strait of Hormuz collapse, the US–China tariff pause, and paper/pulp disruption — a 30–90 day outlook with scenarios and business implications.
